$comment: DRAFT for Stage 0 review. $id is a placeholder: the rigfile.dev domain is not yet claimed (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §17 Q6). Source of truth for structure: RIGFILE_PLAN.md §6 and §9.5. Items marked 'PROPOSED' are additions not present in the plan; each is listed in docs/merge-semantics.md under 'Proposed schema changes'. JSON Schema cannot express cross-field or cross-file rules (pinning of free-form args, model-name references, layer merging, real secret detection); those are listed as validator rules in docs/merge-semantics.md.
title: Rigfile manifest (rigfile.yaml), apiVersion rigfile.dev/v1
description: Declarative description of an AI working environment. Contains no secret values, ever.

^x-.description: Vendor/tooling extension keys. Ignored by Rigfile. Must still not contain secrets (enforced by the validator, not this schema).

license.description: SPDX license identifier or expression, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0.

from.description: Layers this rig inherits, in order (earlier = lower layer). rigfile/base-secure is always implied and is applied first; listing it only pins its version. It cannot be removed (see docs/merge-semantics.md).

targets.description: Which AI tools this rig supports. Targets outside `include` (or inside `exclude`) get a warning, not an error.

instructions.description: Markdown instruction sections, written to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md / .cursor/rules depending on target.

skills.description: SKILL.md folders (Agent Skills format). Claude Code reads ~/.claude/skills, Codex reads ~/.agents/skills; the adapter writes to each.

agents.description: Subagents. Claude Code uses Markdown+frontmatter; Codex uses TOML. Portable definition in the rig is Markdown; adapters convert or skip with a note.

commands.description: Slash commands / reusable prompts. Codex has deprecated custom prompts, so the Codex adapter maps commands to skills.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers keyed by name. Executable servers must be version-pinned (validator rule, docs/merge-semantics.md).

hooks.description: Lifecycle hooks. Prefer builtin: hooks (native binary, identical on every OS).

secrets.description: Declarations only, never values. Key = secret ref path without the secret:// scheme.

gateways.description: Local protocol bridges, e.g. to expose an OpenAI-style server to a client that needs a different API.

overrides.description: Per-target replacements/additions. Keys are target names.

private.description: Paths that are never published and only synced between the owner's own machines.

rigRef.description: owner/name with an optional version or range: jiaxu/python-dev@^2, rigfile/base-secure@1.0.0

os.description: Restrict an item to these operating systems. Omitted = all. `wsl` is a detected sub-case of `linux` and is not a separate value (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §4).

plainText.description: Free text that must not look like a secret. This is a cheap floor, not the scanner: the real check is the `scan` module (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §5.2, §8.1b).

secretLooking.$comment: Known secret shapes (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §8.1b). Also matches obviously-fake corpus values such as sk-ant-TESTTESTTEST..., by design.

secretRef.description: Pointer resolved only at runtime on the user's machine, e.g. secret://alpaca/api_key

secretPath.description: A secret ref path without the scheme, e.g. alpaca/api_key

rigPath.description: Path to a file INSIDE the rig, relative to the rig root. Forward slashes only; no absolute paths, drive letters, `~`, or `..`.

hostPath.description: Path or glob that refers to the USER'S MACHINE (permissions, cwd). Forward slashes only. Start with ${HOME}/, ${CONFIG_DIR}/, ${APP_DATA}/, `~/`, a system absolute path such as /etc/..., or be project-relative (no prefix, `./`, or `**/`). Hard-coded user homes (/Users/..., /home/..., C:\...) are rejected. The platform layer expands per OS; per-tool syntax is applied by adapters (docs/platforms.md §4).

hostPattern.description: Hostname, optionally with a leading wildcard label and optional port: api.example.com, *.example.com, data.example.com:443

itemMeta.$comment: Properties common to items that can be restricted. Repeated per item via allOf because JSON Schema cannot share a property set without unevaluatedProperties.

merge.description: Inserted as a marked section; never replaces user content. Other strategies (e.g. a Rigfile-owned file imported via @) are an open design question, see docs/targets/claude-code.md §3.

ref.description: External skill, e.g. skills.sh/anthropics/pdf@1.0.3. Must be pinned to publish publicly (validator rule).

envMap.description: Environment for a server process. Values are literals or secret refs. Variables whose NAME looks credential-like MUST be secret refs.

args.description: The package version MUST be pinned inside args (e.g. pkg@1.4.2). The schema cannot verify this; the validator does.

url.description: Remote MCP servers must use HTTPS (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §8.3). No credentials in the URL.

auth.description: `oauth` triggers the guided login (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §7.4). `bearer` is PROPOSED (not in the plan's §6.1): requires `bearer_token`. Codex maps it to bearer_token_env_var / http_headers_helper; Claude Code to a header.

headers.description: Static headers. Credential-like header names must be secret refs.

hookEvent.description: Canonical event names. Mapping to native names and per-target support: docs/targets/*.md. Events a target lacks are skipped with a visible note.

hookRunOne.description: Either a built-in (code inside the rigfile binary, identical on every OS) or a path to a script inside the rig.

tool.description: Canonical tool name: bash, powershell, read, edit, write, glob, grep, web_fetch, web_search, agent, mcp, mcp:<server>, mcp:<server>:<tool>, or *.

command.description: Glob against the shell command, e.g. 'git commit*'.

oneOf.description: Per-OS script. A missing OS means the hook is skipped on that OS and flagged on the plan screen.

permissionRule.description: Exactly one of read / edit / bash / web_fetch / mcp, plus optional reason/os/targets.

bash.description: Command prefix/glob, e.g. 'git push*'. Argument-constraining patterns are fragile in Claude Code (see docs/targets/claude-code.md §8).

permissions.description: Canonical allow/ask/deny. Deny always wins across layers and cannot be removed by a later layer (docs/merge-semantics.md). Adapters translate to each tool's native syntax; note that Codex `allow` runs commands outside its sandbox.

packageRef.description: Package name with optional version pin (name or name@version). Includes scoped npm names.

tools.description: Host tools to install. `common` uses logical names resolved via catalog/tools.yaml. The per-OS blocks are the escape hatch when the catalog has no mapping.

obtain_url.description: Where the user creates/rotates this secret.

hosts.description: Owner host binding (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §7.3 rule 3, §7.2 Level 2): the only destinations this secret may be sent to. PROPOSED as a manifest field; the plan says the binding is 'declared in the manifest' but §6.1 shows no field for it.

method.description: Defaults are provider-specific; `vendor-cli` runs the vendor's own login command (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §7.4).

modelApi.description: Wire protocol a server speaks or a gateway exposes. `openai` is the plan's name and is an alias of `openai-chat`. Research showed the distinction matters: Codex custom providers accept only the Responses API (docs/targets/codex.md §9), Claude Code needs Anthropic Messages (docs/targets/claude-code.md §9), and mlx_lm.server speaks only OpenAI chat completions.

loopbackHost.description: Model servers and gateways bind to loopback only (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §9.5 security rules).

modelWhen.description: Hardware/OS selector. All present keys must match; `{}` matches anything.

engine_version.description: Pinned engine version. The validator requires it for public rigs.

model.description: Hugging Face repo id (org/name) or an Ollama tag (name:tag). Publisher org is shown on the plan screen (typosquat defense).

revision.description: Source revision: 40-hex commit SHA for Hugging Face repos. Downloads are pinned and hash-verified. The validator requires it for HF-hosted models on public rigs.

weights_format.description: Only safe formats are allowed (RIGFILE_PLAN.md §9.5). Pickle-based formats and trust_remote_code are deliberately not expressible in a rig; opting in is a local, per-model user decision.

args.description: Engine flags without the leading `--`, e.g. prompt-cache-size. Host, port and model are structured elsewhere and may not appear here.

role.description: Logical role resolved via catalog/models.yaml for this machine, e.g. local-coder. Explicit `variants` (if present) take precedence.

purpose.description: What the rig uses this model for, e.g. summaries, commit-messages, simple-subagents, fallback.

autostart.description: Run as a per-user service (launchd / systemd --user / Windows task). Requires the user's explicit approval on the plan screen.

variants.description: First match for this machine wins; the user can override on the plan screen.

license_ack.description: SPDX id shown on the plan screen. Weights are downloaded from the source and never re-hosted.

engine.description: Only litellm is named in the plan. NOTE: Anthropic states it does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway (docs/targets/claude-code.md §9); rigs using this for Claude Code are experimental.

expose.description: PROPOSED: the API this gateway presents to clients (e.g. anthropic-messages for Claude Code, openai-responses for Codex). Not in the plan's §9.5 example.

routing.description: Translated per target where the tool supports it. Cross-references (fallback_on_limit must name a key of `models`) are checked by the validator.

local_for.description: Task classes routed to the local model: commit-messages, summaries, subagent:<name>, ...

overrideBlock.description: Per-target additions/replacements. Same content categories as the root, without identity fields. Layer/override precedence: docs/merge-semantics.md.
